description:
Read worktree listings through the shared Git module and remove the command's private porcelain parser.

## Background

The worktree command currently starts Git itself and parses entries into a private `GitWorktreeEntry`, omitting detached and bare entries without branches. The module already owns porcelain parsing. An external data store can retain a selected checkout for coordination, so the command must use that already-resolved authority.

The prior plan incorrectly promised a preserved `WORKTREE_LIST_ERROR` code. The existing shared `RequiresGitError` represents a missing checkout; no command-specific classifier or wrapper is needed.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: Worktree listing uses `list_worktrees()` on the already-resolved selected checkout, including relocated external-store context through `write_checkout()`, and still omits entries without a branch. The private porcelain parser, `GitWorktreeEntry` and their two parser unit tests are removed; no listing process starts outside the Git module.
- [hard] REQ-02: Existing Git-checkout output, filtering and external-store identity behavior remain unchanged, with the current worktree-list CLI tests passing.
- [hard] REQ-03: A missing checkout returns the existing `RequiresGitError(GitRequirementGap::NoRepository)`: `REQUIRES_GIT`, exit 10 and canonical remediation. Dispatch declares `raises [RequiresGit]`; other Git failures propagate. CLI coverage owns the mapping and remedy, while the existing status-row census and generated reference reflect the shared contract.

## Notes

DEC-26 extends the shared worktree Git-requirement contract to listing. Reuse supplied checkout facts without adding discovery; sibling context reuse belongs to the invocation-layout mechanism. Historical planning evidence remains in version history.
title: Worktree list reads worktrees through the module
